verses.1: And let Haggai Neviya and Zekhariya Bar-Adoya remember them for the sake of the Jews who live in Judea and in Jerusalem, in the name of the God of Israel.
verses.2: Bedarin, Zerubavel Bar-Shalitiel, Yeshua Bar-Yozadak, and their followers went to the house of God in Jerusalem. Along with them were also Nebyaya, who were also from God’s people.
verses.3: At that time, I will give them a gift beyond the river. I will place it in their hands, and they will be able to use it for their own benefit. And we will say to them, “This is a gift for you; it will be useful for your growth and development.”
verses.4: Edien, as we have said, told them that their names were Gubraya di-Dana binyana baniin.
verses.5: And their eyes were set upon the heads of the Jews. They did not allow them to live, until they could be used for their own purposes. Adayin Yithivun Nishthvana was also affected by this.
verses.6: Parshgen igartá di-shlach tathanai pachat abar-nahara, and shetar boznay. And its construction was done on the other side of the river, over Daryos, king.
verses.7: “Pithgamah shalakhu aloyhi vekidanah, as it is written in the text for Daryavesh, king Shlomo.”
verses.8: Let it be known to the king that in the land of Judea, there is a kingdom called “Medinat.” It is built on a rock, and it will be destroyed by the hands of those who serve it. They will be defeated by their own hands.
verses.9: Adian, we ask you to go ahead and do so. I say to them, “Please give them some taste of what’s in the house that’s meant for cultivation. And also, give them something that can be used for planting.”
verses.10: And even though their names are not written down, we still ask them to know that their names are recorded at the beginning of their stories.
verses.11: And they said these words as a curse. They meant to say, “We are servants of Elah-Shamya and Ar’a. We live in the house of the king. He was the son of Danah Shaginian. And the king of Israel was his son.”
verses.12: From them came those who were angry with the goddess Elah. They were led by Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon. In their homes and in their cities, they were hidden away. Their people was exiled to Babylon.
verses.13: In the year of Khorsh Malaka, in Babylon, Khorsh Malaka had a taste of the house of Elah.
verses.14: And even Manaya, who lived in the house of Elaah, along with Kaspa, who was from Nebuchadnezzar’s kingdom. They were taken away from their homes in Jerusalem. They were also taken to Babylon, where they became slaves. They were given a name: Pеха Шамей.
verses.15: And he said to her, “Tell Manaya that one of her children is in a prison in Jerusalem. And that a house will be built for her there.”
verses.16: From Edin Sheshbatzar, to the place where Yahweh dwells. From that place in Jerusalem, and from there to Kanan, it is built. It’s not complete yet.
verses.17: And now, on this day, good things will be brought about in the house of God in Babylon. This is what the Lord has decided for us. May God bless the house of God in Jerusalem. And may the Lord send His judgment upon Denmark.
